review: First text pass of B462-B470, including each printed vehicle row, location codes, terrain multipliers and mount categories. Values retain compact source notation; independent visual verification, cross-reference resolution and executable behavior remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Powered vehicles use equal strength and health capacity derived from their listed profile, with the machine package and nonliving injury rules; they are persistent objects, not disposable attack modifiers.
An unpowered profile has zero strength and the listed health capacity, with homogeneous injury treatment; its draft creatures or rowers retain their own strength and fatigue.
Store reliability separately from handling and stability, and resolve combustible, flammable and explosive flags through the corresponding damage procedures.

Keep acceleration and maximum velocity distinct, in yards per second per turn and yards per second respectively; the reference uses twice velocity for miles per hour and acceleration divided by ten for terrestrial gravities.

Loaded and payload weights use two-thousand-pound tons. Subtract payload from loaded weight for fueled empty weight; subtract occupants from payload for available cargo, using actual mass or the explicit one-tenth-ton-per-person simplification.
Crew and passenger capacity are separate from mass capacity; record accommodations and sealed, pressure and vacuum protection independently.
Preserve directional and location-specific armor instead of taking a single maximum; vehicle catalogue notes determine the meaning of each paired value.
Distinguish fuel-limited miles, provision-limited travel, creature-fatigue-limited travel and authored exotic drives; an absent numeric range is not infinite supplies.
Water profiles declare minimum safe depth, aircraft minimum airborne speed; zero stall permits hovering rather than an absent constraint.
Represent the general sixty-to-seventy-percent ground/air cruising guidance separately from the specific terrain and aircraft procedures on B466; explicitly select the applicable procedure.

Animal or oar propulsion can sustain about three-quarters maximum speed with hiking fatigue; maximum speed uses running fatigue and is sustainable only briefly. Halve maximum speed when the relevant propulsion creatures fall below one-third fatigue.
Endurance hours equal range miles divided by cruising miles per hour; zero speed is rejected for this calculation, and time, fuel and provisions are committed once.

Travel beyond a day requires provisions; the reference allowance is twelve pounds per person daily. Before technology five, ordinary stored provisions last at most a month; later preserved supplies require actual inventory.
A convoy travels at eighty percent of its slowest member's speed, or the full slowest speed on successful leadership; repeat the check daily for long trips and persist each day's result.
Hazardous operations require the relevant vehicle control skill; author the ongoing-hazard check cadence and situational facts before committing time or a roll.
Apply handling to control checks. Apply visibility penalties only when collision risk makes visibility relevant; retain skill-specific and maneuver modifiers.

Failure margin no greater than stability produces a minor problem; greater failure produces a major one, while critical failure guarantees disaster. Noncombat consequences require an explicit authored outcome contract.
A discretionary second control attempt requires a specific recovery action and penalty; it must not silently erase a critical disaster or offer unlimited retries.

When both master and crew checks are required, combine the master's shiphandling margin and average crew-skill check margin by averaging; define fractional-margin and critical-result handling explicitly before implementation.
Off road, a road-dependent vehicle uses min(maximum velocity, four times acceleration) as the input to terrain speed; on-road dirt and paved terrain retain their respective multipliers.
Rails count as good terrain for rail-dependent vehicles; movement off rails is illegal rather than merely slower.
Flat-out ground travel may increase safe cruising speed by up to sixty percent, with authored hourly control checks for mishaps; do not multiply top velocity a second time.
Apply the hiking weather procedures to ground travel; sleds and snowmobiles use skating behavior on ice and skiing behavior on snow.

Powered water travel uses twice maximum velocity in miles per hour; ideal sailing uses the same rate, modified by authored wind. Sustained rowing uses one-and-a-half times maximum velocity and the shared crew fatigue ledger.
Apply currents directly to travel velocity, and authored heavy-sea reductions separately. Storm-driven unpowered vessels can require both captain and crew checks.

Depth below draft grounds the vessel. Refloating requires an actual tide, ballast or payload change; area knowledge recalls depth and sea navigation reads charts, without manufacturing missing world facts.

Aircraft cruise at maximum velocity times 1.6 miles per hour; full speed is twice velocity and consumes fifty percent more fuel. Define consumption per time consistently with printed range and reduced full-speed range.

Supersonic aircraft with movement at least 360 need altitude at least fifteen thousand feet for their full listed speed. Low-altitude limits in the approximate 350-400 range require an authored aircraft/environment limit.
Require authored control checks for difficult landings, low-altitude fast flight and mountain routes; balloons and airships use wind and storm constraints comparable to sailing craft.
Powered aircraft ground taxi normally permits at most two-thirds stall velocity; an exceptional ground drive must be explicit.
Time to a chosen velocity is 0.10 times velocity divided by acceleration in gravities, in seconds; a 90000 velocity change at 1.5 gravities takes 6000 seconds.
Coasting time in hours is 0.5 times distance in miles divided by velocity in yards per second; reject zero velocity for nonzero distance.
Use the supplied approximate astronomical conversions: one orbital-distance unit is ninety-three million miles, a light-year is 5.865 trillion miles, and a parsec is 3.26 light-years.
For reaction drives the printed maximum velocity is the total velocity-change budget; each acceleration and deceleration spends that shared budget, including orbital transfers.

Low terrestrial orbit requires velocity change 8700; escaping from orbit costs an additional 3600. Scale both by sqrt(planet mass / planet radius) in terrestrial units and require thrust acceleration greater than local gravity for liftoff.
A travel assessment includes departure, cruise acceleration and destination deceleration before committing fuel; the printed example spends 3600+90000+88500 from 200000, leaving 17900.

An authorized drive without reaction-mass limits needs acceleration above local gravity to depart. Constant-thrust travel time is sqrt(50.8 times distance in millions of miles divided by acceleration in gravities), in hours.
Faster-than-light speed, limits and any defensive fields are explicit campaign-authored drive parameters; a catalogue exotic marker alone grants none of them.

Vehicle movement occurs on its operator's turn. Move or move-and-attack controls it; another maneuver or operator incapacity preserves the previous speed and course until the applicable uncontrolled-motion procedure intervenes.
Other occupants act on their own turns and must be at the relevant station; electronics require concentration and weapons an appropriate attack maneuver. Preserve individual defense eligibility.
Bailing onto ground causes collision with an immovable object at vehicle speed, plus falling damage when airborne. Jumping between vehicles uses dexterity or jumping with relative-speed penalties.
At or below acceleration, use ordinary movement restrictions; above it use high-speed movement with control checks replacing dexterity checks. Integrate vehicle footprints with tactical occupancy.
Increase velocity by at most acceleration per turn; a diving flyer can add ten times local gravity in terrestrial units.
A powered wheeled ground vehicle safely sheds five yards per second per turn.
Animal-drawn, tracked, walking and slithering ground vehicles safely shed ten yards per second per turn.
Most air and water vehicles safely shed max(1,5+handling) yards per second per turn; exceeding the safe rate invokes high-speed control and loss-of-control consequences.
Risky maneuvers, obstacles, knockback and major damage trigger control checks. Resolve the triggering event once even if several integration layers observe it.
Every failed control check clears accumulated aim and penalizes attacks from the vehicle by the failure margin until the operator's next turn.
Air-control failure within stability loses five yards altitude and ten velocity, with stall and ground collision checked against the resulting state.

Air-control failure exceeding stability or critical failure creates uncontrolled flight: a climbing vehicle stalls and falls, otherwise dives at maximum speed each turn. Subsequent recovery requires piloting at -5.
Minor ground loss fails the intended turn or randomly veers left/right when no turn was attempted; collision depends on actual authored obstacles and position.
Major or critical ground loss crashes after skidding or rolling one-third current velocity in distance; apply falling damage based on velocity at loss of control.

Minor space/underwater loss continues or veers instead of the intended maneuver and fails obstacle avoidance. Preserve the printed submarine depth change of five yards with an explicit signed-depth convention. Major/critical loss requires reliability to avoid authored stress damage.
Minor water loss uses ground veering; standing open-deck occupants each roll strength or strength-based seamanship to avoid going overboard.
Major/critical water loss capsizes and throws deck occupants overboard. Only specifically unsinkable profiles permit righting; other vessels sink.
Mounted attacks require the occupant to man the station. Targeting bonuses usually require aim; example optical and computerized systems give +2 and +3 only when actually fitted.
A vehicle with appropriate limbs can punch, kick or grapple using the shared melee procedures and its own physical properties; a generic vehicle profile cannot attack with nonexistent limbs.
Enclosed occupants need a usable firing opening. Shooting through a windshield makes it opaque until a ready action clears it, and may breach sealed, pressurized or vacuum-protected compartments.
Moving-platform penalties depend on ride and mount, using B548. A nonoperator suffers another -2 after vehicle dodging, or -4 when flying.

Combined accuracy, extra aim, targeting and bracing bonuses cannot exceed stability on an unstable moving platform unless mount or sights are stabilized. Include stationary bobbing/turbulence; in space apply the cap while maneuvering, not straight coasting.
Ranged speed penalties use apparent crossing motion; a target moving approximately directly toward or away does not receive a crossing-speed penalty merely from large closing speed.
An operator using a handheld weapon must move-and-attack and takes the worse of -2 or weapon bulk. Do not apply that specific penalty to mounted weapons, ramming or vehicle melee.
Vehicle dodge is floor(operator control skill / 2 + handling); skill fourteen and handling one gives eight. It is an operator action, not an additional independent vehicle turn.
An occupant free to move may dodge an attack specifically targeting them, but cannot defend against a stray or penetrating shot; restraints and maneuver restrictions remain applicable.
Default attacks target the body; deliberate or random locations must exist and be exposed. Resolve the B554 location-specific consequences rather than ordinary character anatomy.
Exposed riders have no vehicle cover. Open or windowed cabins protect legs, groin and half the torso; shooting into or out of a window adds -1 unless leaning out.
Ramming uses a slam attack with operator control skill and shared collision damage. Forcing a vehicle off-road instead uses side-on collision damage as knockback only.
Without an operator, one/two-wheel vehicles and two/three-legged walkers roll over. Others continue and roll one die each turn: six or a result above stability causes loss of control.
Regaining control requires actually reaching the controls; an incapacitated former operator obstructing them imposes at least -2, with authored additional penalty and access time.

Penetration below a floating hull's waterline, any balloon/airship body penetration, or submerged-vehicle penetration outside an external mount creates a leak. Reuse bleeding timing with crew skill replacing first aid for patching, without creating character blood loss.
Optional scale ten or one hundred divides resistance, health capacity and damage dice with half-up rounding. Expand damage multipliers to dice first; armor divisors remain unchanged.

For scaled damage below one die, fractions through one-quarter become 1d-3, through one-half 1d-2, and larger fractions 1d-1. Specify behavior for zero damage and fixed damage modifiers before allowing unsupported inputs.
After scaled combat multiply remaining health by the scale factor once; retain the scale on encounter state so save/load or repeated settlement cannot rescale twice.

Technology 8 mount: Uses handheld-weapon attack rules through an actual arm or striker mount.
Technology 3 mount: Uses a fixed arc but does not cap attack skill by operator control skill; crew can redirect the weapon with its carriage equipment.
Technology 1 mount: Can swivel and elevate, but provides no vehicle protection to weapon or crew.
Technology 7 mount: Retains exposed crew and weapon while stabilization changes moving-fire penalties.
Technology 1 mount: Aims by vehicle direction; use the lower of gunner and control skill within the declared fixed arc.
Technology 6 mount: Uses fixed-mount rules with accuracy reduced by one; external loads count toward encumbrance.
Technology 5 mount: Rotates independently of vehicle facing; record its actual arc and power requirements.
Technology 7 mount: Adds stabilization that maintains aim independently of vehicle motion.

The sled requires fourteen dogs; chariot and wagon two horses each, coach four. Purchase and fatigue of animals remain separate from the unpowered chassis.

With its forty-eight-foot trailer, the tractor uses handling -3, stability 4 and movement 1/30 road-dependent. The trailer independently has health capacity 100, payload 24 tons, size +5 and armor 3; missing statistics need authored values, not invented defaults.
The armored carrier has resistance 50 front and 35 elsewhere, and a roof-mounted exposed 7.62 mm or .50 weapon requiring selection and its own ammunition inventory.
The galley rowing profile requires fifty rowers. Under fair-wind sail it uses movement 1/4 and provision-limited range; its ram adds one collision damage per die.
The cargo sailship is wind-driven and its printed weight includes ballast; do not subtract that weight twice when calculating available payload or grounding recovery.
The advanced rotorcraft has resistance 20 on its rotor and 5 on every other location.
The orbital transport uses a reaction drive for orbit and reentry; at technology ten or higher its price is seventy million rather than three hundred fifty million.

The two exotic spacecraft use reactionless or gravity propulsion, with light-speed maximum or an explicitly lower campaign cap. Faster-than-light capability and force fields require separate authored installations.

The space freighter includes all-around multispectral sight with ten telescopic levels and targeting radar range five hundred thousand yards; implement the underlying perception traits before claiming this equipment complete.

Each of the two independent turrets can purchase a five-hundred-thousand energy cannon: burning damage 6d times 5 with divisor 2, accuracy 10, ranges 100000/300000, rate 4 and recoil 1. Optional weapons do not appear merely because turrets exist.

The sports-car location string is printed GW4 rather than the usual G4W. Preserve transcription and resolve the suffix quantity through a rendered-page audit before accepting the executable location model.

vehicle_data_encoding.capacity: suffix u marks unpowered, zero strength; otherwise strength equals health capacity
vehicle_data_encoding.movement: acceleration/velocity; suffix r road-dependent, t rail-dependent; c light speed
vehicle_data_encoding.clearance: water draft in feet or aircraft stall in yards per second; dash not supplied
vehicle_data_encoding.range_miles: F uses propulsion-creature fatigue; dash requires provision or drive-specific handling
vehicle_data_encoding.flags: reliability c/f/x; occupants A/S/P/V; case-sensitive location notation as individually inventoried
vehicle_data_encoding.precision: decimal strings preserve transcribed values until validated conversion
